title: Fix pluralisation in report text summary
body:
## Summary

`advisory-watch report` prints lines such as `5 contracts, 3 unique Wasm, 1 Stellar Asset Contracts` and `1 contracts in 1 Wasm`. Singular counts should read `1 Stellar Asset Contract` and `1 contract`.

## Where

`NetworkReport::to_text` in `crates/core/src/report.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Counts of 1 use the singular noun for `contract` and `Stellar Asset Contract`
- [ ] Counts of 0 and 2+ use the plural
- [ ] A unit test in `report.rs` covers 0, 1 and 2
- [ ] The example output in `docs/src/guides/network-report.md` is updated

## Tech stack

Rust

title: Print a summary line after multi-target scan output
body:
## Summary

When `scan` is given several `--wasm` or `--contract-id` values, the text output lists each target but gives no total. Add a final line such as `3 targets: 1 possible, 1 unknown, 1 not-matched`.

## Where

`ScanReport::to_text` in `crates/core/src/report.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Summary line printed only when there is more than one target
- [ ] Counts by overall status, in the order possible, unknown, not-matched, not-applicable, omitting zero counts
- [ ] JSON output unchanged
- [ ] Test in `report.rs` and an end-to-end test in `crates/cli/tests/cli.rs` using two fixtures

## Tech stack

Rust

title: Accept a directory for scan --wasm
body:
## Summary

Workspaces with several contracts produce several `.wasm` files under `target/wasm32v1-none/release/`. Let `--wasm` take a directory and scan every `*.wasm` file directly inside it (not recursive).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `advisory-watch scan --wasm fixtures/wasm` scans all three fixtures
- [ ] Files are scanned in sorted order so output is stable
- [ ] A directory with no `.wasm` files is an error (exit code 2) with a clear message
- [ ] End-to-end test in `crates/cli/tests/cli.rs`
- [ ] `docs/src/reference/cli.md` regenerated and `docs/src/guides/ci.md` mentions the option

## Tech stack

Rust, clap

title: Show cliver and other build meta keys in scan output
body:
## Summary

`stellar contract build` writes `cliver` (Stellar CLI version) and lets users add keys with `--meta`, for example `source_repo` and `commit_sha`. These help a reviewer find the source of a deployed contract. Today `scan` shows only `rssdkver`, `rsver` and the protocol.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TargetReport` gets a `meta` field with all `contractmetav0` entries (JSON output)
- [ ] Text output shows `cliver`, `source_repo` and `commit_sha` when present
- [ ] Values are printed as-is; the docs say they are self-reported and unverified
- [ ] Unit test with a synthetic module that has these keys (see `test_support` in `crates/core/src/lib.rs`)
- [ ] `docs/src/reference/output.md` updated

## Tech stack

Rust

title: Add cargo-binstall metadata for release binaries
body:
## Summary

The release workflow publishes `advisory-watch-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` (and `.zip` on Windows). Adding `[package.metadata.binstall]` to `crates/cli/Cargo.toml` lets users run `cargo binstall soroban-advisory-watch` instead of compiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pkg-url`, `bin-dir` and `pkg-fmt` match the asset names and archive layout in `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- [ ] Windows override uses `zip`
- [ ] `docs/src/install.md` documents the command

## Tech stack

Cargo metadata, GitHub Actions

## Reference

https://github.com/cargo-bins/cargo-binstall/blob/main/SUPPORT.md

title: Add CSV output for report
body:
## Summary

Teams want to open network reports in a spreadsheet. Add `--format csv` to `report`, with one row per contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Columns: `contract_id,wasm_hash,sdk_version,status,possible_advisories` (advisory ids joined with `;`)
- [ ] Stellar Asset Contracts and error rows included with `status` `not-applicable` and `error`
- [ ] `--format csv` on `scan` is rejected with a clear error, or also implemented with the same columns
- [ ] End-to-end test using `examples/inventory.jsonl` and `examples/wasm`
- [ ] `docs/src/reference/output.md` documents the columns

## Tech stack

Rust

title: Add signal for slice and gen_range host imports (GHSA-96xm-fv9w-pf3f)
body:
## Summary

GHSA-96xm-fv9w-pf3f only matters for contracts that call `Bytes::slice`, `Vec::slice` or `Prng::gen_range` for `u64`. In soroban-sdk 25.0.1 these call the host functions `bytes_slice` (`b.f`), `vec_slice` (`v.c`) and `prng_u64_in_inclusive_range` (`p.1`), per `soroban-env-common/env.json`. A Wasm that imports none of them never reaches that host code.

Add a signal `imports-slice-or-range-host-functions` and attach it to the advisory in `advisories/annotations.toml`.

## Care needed

- Other SDK methods may call the same host functions. Check `rs-soroban-sdk` source for every caller of these three functions in the affected versions and document them in the signal's `limits` text.
- Signals never change status. `observed: false` must not produce `not-matched`.
- Confirm the export names are the same in soroban-sdk 22.x and 23.x.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Signal implemented in `crates/core/src/signals.rs` with a `limits` explanation backed by the source review
- [ ] Annotation updated; `annotation_signals_are_known` test passes
- [ ] Unit tests for observed and not observed
- [ ] `docs/src/how-it-works.md` signal table updated

## Tech stack

Rust, Soroban SDK internals

title: Fetch advisories from OSV.dev with an `advisories update` command
body:
## Summary

The binary bundles the advisories known at release time. New ones need `--osv FILE`. Add `advisory-watch advisories update` that downloads current OSV records for Soroban crates and stores them in a cache directory, and make `scan` and `report` load that cache automatically.

## Design

- OSV API: `POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query` with `{"package":{"ecosystem":"crates.io","name":"soroban-sdk"}}`. Query at least `soroban-sdk`, `soroban-sdk-macros`, `soroban-spec`, `soroban-env-host`, `soroban-env-common`.
- Cache location: platform cache dir (for example `dirs::cache_dir()`), overridable with `--advisory-cache`.
- Cached records override bundled ones with the same id (this already works through `AdvisoryDb::add_osv_json`).
- Networking stays in `crates/cli`; reuse the `ureq` agent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `advisories update` downloads, validates (parses) and writes records; prints how many were added or changed
- [ ] `scan`/`report` use the cache when present; `--no-cache` disables it
- [ ] Tests use a local mock HTTP server (see `spawn_rpc` in `crates/cli/tests/cli.rs`), no real network
- [ ] Docs: `docs/src/guides/new-advisory.md` and `docs/src/reference/cli.md`

## Tech stack

Rust, ureq, OSV schema

title: Verify and document the Hubble inventory query
body:
## Summary

`examples/hubble-contract-instances.sql` was written from the Hubble data dictionary and stellar-etl source, but has not been run against BigQuery. Run it, fix it if needed, and record what it costs.

## Questions to answer

- Is the table path `crypto-stellar.crypto_stellar.contract_data` correct?
- Does `contract_key_type = 'ScValTypeScvLedgerKeyContractInstance'` match the stored values?
- How are archived (evicted) instance entries represented? Should they be excluded?
- How many bytes does the query scan? Can a partition filter on `closed_at` reduce it without missing contracts?
- Is there a cheaper silver table (for example `contract_data_snapshot`) that gives the same result?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Query runs and the export works unchanged with `advisory-watch report --inventory`
- [ ] SQL file updated; the "not yet run" note replaced with the date run and bytes scanned
- [ ] `docs/src/guides/network-report.md` updated with the findings
- [ ] Row count and run date noted in the PR (no contract lists needed)

## Tech stack

BigQuery SQL, Stellar Hubble

title: Resolve the exact soroban-sdk-macros version from Cargo.lock
body:
## Summary

For `soroban-sdk-macros` advisories the Wasm only gives a lower bound, so results are `possible` with low confidence. When scanning a local build, the user usually has the `Cargo.lock`. Add `scan --lockfile Cargo.lock` to read exact versions for crates the Wasm does not record.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parse `Cargo.lock` (v3 and v4) with the `toml` crate already in the dependency tree, or the `cargo-lock` crate
- [ ] With a lock file, `soroban-sdk-macros` and third-party crates such as `soroban-fixed-point-math` are matched exactly; confidence `high`, `version_recorded: true`
- [ ] The lock file's `soroban-sdk` version must equal `rssdkver`; if not, print a warning and ignore the lock file for that target
- [ ] A lock file listing two versions of a crate uses all of them (any affected version gives `possible`)
- [ ] Tests with the lock files in `fixtures/contracts/*/Cargo.lock`
- [ ] Docs updated (`guides/ci.md`, `how-it-works.md`)

## Tech stack

Rust

title: Check rssdkver git revision against release tags
body:
## Summary

`rssdkver` holds the SDK version and git revision, for example `25.0.1#941448079eccf95627d2ffea13ba268e305a9077`. A crates.io release has a fixed revision. A different revision means the contract was built from a git dependency or a fork, where the version number may not describe the code.

Add a bundled table of `version -> revision` for soroban-sdk releases and add a note to the target when the revision does not match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Script in `scripts/` that builds the table from crates.io or GitHub tags (document the source)
- [ ] Table covers 22.0.0 onward and is compiled into the core crate
- [ ] Target JSON gets `sdk_revision_matches_release: true|false|null` (null when the version is not in the table)
- [ ] Text output prints a warning on mismatch
- [ ] Status rules unchanged
- [ ] Tests use the two fixture revisions, which come from crates.io builds

## Tech stack

Rust, crates.io API or git tags

title: Batch getLedgerEntries requests in report
body:
## Summary

`report` downloads each unique Wasm with its own `getLedgerEntries` call. The RPC method accepts many keys per request, so a network report with thousands of Wasm hashes makes far more requests than needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `RpcClient` gets `wasm_by_hashes(&[&str]) -> Vec<(hash, Result<Vec<u8>>)>`
- [ ] `report` fetches uncached Wasm in batches; batch size flag `--rpc-batch-size` with a default no higher than the limit documented by Stellar RPC (find and cite it)
- [ ] Missing entries in a batch are reported per hash, not as a batch failure
- [ ] Downloaded bytes still checked against their hash
- [ ] Unit tests with the replay transport; end-to-end test with the mock server

## Tech stack

Rust, Stellar RPC

title: Retry and rate-limit RPC calls
body:
## Summary

Public RPC providers rate-limit. One HTTP 429 or timeout during a long `report` run currently turns that Wasm into an error.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retry on HTTP 429, 502, 503, 504 and timeouts, with exponential backoff and jitter; honour `Retry-After`
- [ ] `--rpc-retries` (default 3) and `--rpc-max-rps` (default unlimited) flags
- [ ] JSON-RPC errors are not retried
- [ ] Implemented in the CLI's `Transport`; core crate unchanged
- [ ] Tests with a mock server that returns 429 then 200

## Tech stack

Rust, ureq

title: Add a reusable GitHub Action
body:
## Summary

Make CI adoption one step: a composite action in `action.yml` at the repository root, so contract repositories can write:

```yaml
- uses: soroban-advisory-watch/soroban-advisory-watch@v0
  with:
    wasm: target/wasm32v1-none/release/my_contract.wasm
    fail-on: possible
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inputs: `wasm` (path or glob), `fail-on`, `version` (release tag, default latest), `format`
- [ ] Downloads the release binary for the runner OS and checks it against `SHA256SUMS`; no compiling
- [ ] Writes the text report to the job summary (`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`)
- [ ] A workflow in this repository runs the action against `fixtures/wasm`
- [ ] `docs/src/guides/ci.md` documents it

## Tech stack

GitHub Actions (composite), bash

title: Add SARIF output for scan
body:
## Summary

GitHub code scanning and many security dashboards read SARIF 2.1.0. Add `--format sarif` to `scan` so results show up in the Security tab of a contract repository.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One SARIF `rule` per advisory (id, summary, help URI = advisory URL)
- [ ] One `result` per `possible` finding; `unknown` findings as `note` level, `not-matched` omitted
- [ ] Location is the Wasm file path
- [ ] Output validates against the SARIF 2.1.0 JSON schema in a test
- [ ] `docs/src/reference/output.md` documents the mapping

Rust, SARIF 2.1.0

title: Publish a JSON Schema for scan and report output

title: Fuzz the Wasm, OSV and inventory parsers
body:
## Summary

The tool reads untrusted input: Wasm from the ledger, RPC responses, OSV files and inventories. Add `cargo-fuzz` targets so crashes and unbounded allocations are found before users hit them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fuzz/` crate with targets for `wasm::analyze`, `AdvisoryDb::add_osv_file_contents`, `inventory::parse` (both formats) and `rpc::executable_from_contract_data_xdr`
- [ ] Seed corpus from `fixtures/wasm`, `advisories/osv` and `examples/inventory.jsonl`
- [ ] Each target runs 10 minutes locally without a crash; any bugs found are fixed with a regression test
- [ ] `docs/src/development.md` explains how to run them

## Tech stack

Rust, cargo-fuzz (nightly)

title: Research: detect overflow-checks setting from Wasm
body:
## Summary

GHSA-96xm-fv9w-pf3f only affects contracts built with `overflow-checks = false`. If the setting can be inferred from the Wasm, the tool could add a signal for it.

## Questions

- With `overflow-checks = true`, rustc inserts checked arithmetic that branches to a panic. Is there a reliable, SDK-independent pattern in the compiled Wasm (for example around the `slice` code paths)?
- How do `opt-level`, `lto` and `wasm-opt` change the pattern?
- What is the false-positive and false-negative rate on the fixture contracts built both ways?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Write-up in `docs/src/research/overflow-checks.md` with the method, the contracts tested, and results
- [ ] Fixture contracts built with both settings added under `fixtures/contracts/`
- [ ] Recommendation: implement as a signal, or not, with reasons
- [ ] No change to status rules

## Tech stack

Rust, Wasm, `wasm-tools`

title: Research: support the ExternalRef contract executable
body:
## Summary

`stellar-xdr` 30 adds a third `ContractExecutable` variant, `ExternalRef(ContractExecutableExternalRef)`. The tool currently reports such contracts as `executable type external-ref is not supported yet`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Find the CAP or protocol change that introduced it and what code such a contract runs
- [ ] Decide how to scan it (follow the reference to a Wasm hash? treat like Stellar Asset Contracts?)
- [ ] Implement in `crates/core/src/rpc.rs` and `inventory.rs`, with tests
- [ ] Document in `docs/src/how-it-works.md`

## Tech stack

Rust, Stellar XDR, CAPs

title: Build an inventory without BigQuery
body:
## Summary

Network reports need an inventory, and the documented route uses Hubble on BigQuery, which needs a Google Cloud account. Add a route that only needs public Stellar infrastructure.

## Options to evaluate

1. Read ledger metadata exported by Galexie (Stellar's ledger exporter) to a data lake, and collect contract instance entries.
2. Follow `createContract` operations and `ContractData` instance changes via Stellar RPC `getTransactions`/`getLedgers` over the RPC retention window, then maintain the list incrementally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Short design note in the PR comparing the options (coverage, time, cost) with sources
- [ ] `advisory-watch inventory build ...` writes a JSONL inventory in the existing format
- [ ] Incremental: a second run only processes new ledgers
- [ ] Tests with recorded ledger data, no live network
- [ ] Docs page under `guides/`

## Tech stack

Rust, Stellar RPC or Galexie, XDR
